_comment: Populated by the first real full-history secrets scan (pub-readiness phase-6, GitHub #200), replacing the Option-A placeholder that stood here with stamp: null. Findings are grouped BY CLASS: 209 findings across five mechanical classes would otherwise produce 209 near-identical rationales, which is how a baseline becomes unreadable and therefore unreviewed. Every count here is DERIVED from the raw reports and the per-class sums are asserted equal to the scan totals before this file is written -- see the note below on why.
_why_the_sums_are_asserted: The first version of this file asserted three classes summing to 127 of 129 gitleaks findings and 78 of 80 trufflehog findings. Four findings were in no class, and the test-key class misattributed its own hits. Nothing caught it: the stamp looked complete and the phase called itself done. The karen gate found it by reconstructing per-file counts from the reports. tools/gate/test_secrets_baseline_arithmetic.py now fails if the per-class sums stop matching the stamped totals, so this cannot drift silently again.

stamp.head: 62f7fb11d1174eafcfbf29ea30dd8e21ca2ea30c
stamp.scope: full history (gitleaks detect --log-opts=--all; trufflehog git file://.)
stamp.verdict: NO TRUE POSITIVES. All 129 gitleaks and 80 trufflehog findings are accounted for across five classes, sums verified. trufflehog verified 0 of 80, which is the strongest single signal: it attempts live validation.
stamp.tooling_note: scripts/security/install_tools.ps1 verifies each downloaded scanner against a SHA256 pinned in the script. Get-FileHash does not resolve in this environment, so the installer FAILED CLOSED rather than installing unverified binaries. The cmdlet was supplied via .NET SHA256 and known-answer tested against the published digest of the empty string before being trusted; the pinned check then passed for both tools. The shim is committed at scripts/security/get_filehash_shim.ps1 so the claim is inspectable rather than narrated.

accepted_findings.rationale: A vcpkg binary-cache manifest: a map from installed file path to its 64-hex ABI hash, 7,366 of them. A generic high-entropy rule reads any 64-hex string as a possible key. The lone sentry-access-token hit is the ABI hash of a Qt6 QtNetwork header -- the rule matched the hash, not a token. These are build-reproducibility digests, published deliberately, and carry no authority.

Deliberately weak keys so the PDF signature / CRL / TSA tests can sign and verify offline. ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED on the second pass: gitleaks reported ZERO private-key hits against the seven PEM fixtures -- its 10 came from the generator (9) and from check_test_key_markers.py's own test module (1), which embeds PKCS8/PKCS1/ENCRYPTED PEM constants as fixtures. trufflehog is the scanner that flagged the PEM files themselves (7 of its 15). check_test_key_markers.py enforces a test marker on committed PEM-bearing files and exits 0, which covers the fixtures -- it does NOT cover the PEM constants inside its own test module, so that one hit rests on inspection, not on that mechanism.

The file pins GitHub Actions to 40-hex commit SHAs, which is the supply-chain hardening this repository requires. A token detector reads 40-hex as a credential. Unverified, and a commit SHA grants nothing.

NEW CLASS, added after the karen gate found these two in no class at all. One is a literal assigned to a field in an encryption round-trip test -- a test password, which is the point of the test. The other is inside a COMMENT, where a quoted example string tripped the rule. Neither authenticates anything.

NEW CLASS, same origin. Both are committed gtest listings, and both hits are trufflehog's Box detector matching the TEST CASE NAME 'CropPageCommandRedoReappliesCrop'. A test name that happens to fit a token's character class is not a token. Unverified.

note: Five classes, 129 + 80 findings, zero true positives. A finding outside these classes is NOT accepted: triage it in triage.md first. Do not widen a class to silence a new file -- that is how a baseline becomes a rubber stamp.
